annotations.text:
TODAY — one task at full size.
The clock, the day bar and the minute count are always visible (time blindness). Steps are pre-broken so starting costs nothing. Everything safe is off this screen; "Waiting on you" stays folded until asked for. Try: tick a step, Not this one, Start.

FOCUS — the app removes itself.
No nav, no search, no counts. Live ring and countdown. "Park a thought" is the intrusive-thought valve so leaving is never the only option, and "Too big — break it down" splits three steps into six. Try: Pause, break it down, park something.

EVERYTHING — three segments replace nine chips, and the list is capped at three with the rest one tap away. Rows, not cards: one line each, 44px targets, red as a 4px rail rather than a wash. Try: the segments, the area row, Show the other two.

PATTERNS — the chart's job is to hand you one sentence. Streaks are off by default; nothing here counts how long something has been late. Settings is six plain-language switches, not a form wall. Try: 7 / 30 days, and the switches.

The palette is carried over hex for hex, light and dark, along with Playfair Display, Inter and the 8/6/4px radii. What changed is how much of the screen may ask for a decision at once — the ten rules at the bottom right are the whole argument.

CALENDAR — the month is now the whole page, not half of it.
Every day cell carries the actual names, so one glance answers "what is coming" without a legend to memorise. Gone: the split layout, the colour key, the daily-habit footnote, the month paragraph and the capture box. What is left is one heading sentence, three buttons and thirty-five days. The day panel only exists once you ask for it. Try: a day, Close, the month arrows, and the Density tweak.
